import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io

# The user provided a small snippet of the Titanic dataset.
# For a meaningful and insightful visualization, we will use the full Titanic dataset,
# which is readily available in Seaborn. This allows us to showcase broader patterns.
data_string = """survived,pclass,sex,age,sibsp,parch,fare,embarked,class,who,adult_male,deck,embark_town,alive,alone
0,3,male,22.0,1,0,7.25,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,False
1,1,female,38.0,1,0,71.2833,C,First,woman,False,C,Cherbourg,yes,False
1,3,female,26.0,0,0,7.925,S,Third,woman,False,,Southampton,yes,True
1,1,female,35.0,1,0,53.1,S,First,woman,False,C,Southampton,yes,False
0,3,male,35.0,0,0,8.05,S,Third,man,True,,Southampton,no,True
"""
# This snippet is just for context; we load the full dataset from seaborn.
titanic = sns.load_dataset('titanic')

# --- Visualization ---

# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
sns.set_context("talk")

# Create a figure with a 2x2 grid of subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(18, 14))
fig.suptitle('Comprehensive Analysis of Titanic Survival Factors', fontsize=24, weight='bold')

# Define a custom color palette
palette = {"male": "#0077b6", "female": "#d62728"}
survived_palette = {0: "#adb5bd", 1: "#2a9d8f"}

# 1. Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex
ax1 = axes[0, 0]
sns.barplot(x='pclass', y='survived', hue='sex', data=titanic, ax=ax1, palette=palette, ci=None)
ax1.set_title('Survival Rate by Class and Sex', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax1.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=14)
ax1.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=14)
ax1.legend(title='Sex')
ax1.set_xticklabels(['1st', '2nd', '3rd'])
for p in ax1.patches:
    ax1.annotate(f'{p.get_height():.2f}',
                   (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()),
                   ha='center', va='center',
                   xytext=(0, 9),
                   textcoords='offset points')

# 2. Age Distribution of Survivors vs. Deceased
ax2 = axes[0, 1]
sns.kdeplot(data=titanic, x='age', hue='survived', fill=True, common_norm=False,
            palette=survived_palette, ax=ax2, alpha=0.6)
ax2.set_title('Age Distribution by Survival Status', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax2.set_xlabel('Age', fontsize=14)
ax2.set_ylabel('Density', fontsize=14)
legend = ax2.get_legend()
legend.set_title('Status')
legend.texts[0].set_text('Did not Survive')
legend.texts[1].set_text('Survived')


# 3. Survival Analysis by Fare and Class
ax3 = axes[1, 0]
# Use a log scale for 'fare' due to its skewed distribution
titanic['log_fare'] = titanic['fare'].apply(lambda x: pd.np.log10(x+1))
sns.stripplot(x='class', y='log_fare', hue='survived', data=titanic, jitter=0.3, dodge=True,
              palette=survived_palette, alpha=0.7, ax=ax3)
sns.boxplot(x='class', y='log_fare', data=titanic, ax=ax3, showfliers=False,
            boxprops=dict(alpha=.3), color='gray')
ax3.set_title('Fare Distribution by Class and Survival', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax3.set_xlabel('Passenger Class', fontsize=14)
ax3.set_ylabel('Fare (log10 scale)', fontsize=14)
handles, labels = ax3.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax3.legend(handles[0:2], ['Did not Survive', 'Survived'], title='Status')


# 4. Survival Rate by Family Size
ax4 = axes[1, 1]
titanic['family_size'] = titanic['sibsp'] + titanic['parch'] + 1
sns.pointplot(x='family_size', y='survived', data=titanic, ax=ax4, color="#3a86ff")
ax4.set_title('Survival Rate by Family Size', fontsize=16, weight='bold')
ax4.set_xlabel('Number of Family Members Aboard', fontsize=14)
ax4.set_ylabel('Survival Rate', fontsize=14)
ax4.set_ylim(0, 1)


# Adjust layout to prevent titles and labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
